commits.message: About Me module now shows the short blurb configurable in the Edit My Account page.

The "Edit My Account" page now saves data correctly to the database.

Data saved (namely the "About Me" blurb) was being saved with a strange
value for field_type in the database. Now, it saves using the GENERAL type
and, as such, can be retrieved by the AboutUserModule.
Fixes a tiny bug with the two previously created modules.

Adds two new modules, UserContributionsModule and UserParticipationModule, for the
express purpose of the CivicCommons.

These must be enabled to show on the User Public Page. To do this, add the modules to the page
in the admin Module Selector.
Fixes some errant redirects.

Organization admins can now either view or select polls based on which link they click.
After creating the poll, it now redirects to the correct location.
Adds in some support for group polls in the database.

Fixes some things in the Image uploading process.

Since we upgraded jQuery in commit dafb028, it broke the image uploading.
I now suspect this is due to the difference in handling CSS3 selectors
between jQuery versions. In older versions, $(":input[@name=tom]") selects
all <input> tags with name="tom". In the latest version, however, the
attribute selector changed to $(":input[name=tom]") to select the same
thing. Consequently, the image uploader was not uploading the image
because the pre-submit method to remove _just the submit button_ now removed
_*all* input fields_. Removing the at-sign seems to have rectified the problem.

So, while here, I figured an upgrade to the jQuery form plugin was in order.

Testing confirms that image uploading works in Firefox and Chrome.

Makes some hefty changes to the install process. Switches steps 3
and 4 so the order is now 3) Database Selection, 4) Admin user. As a
result of this, the PeepAgg.mysql file is no longer edited prior to
execution. [#29 state:resolved].

Also, the installer now checks to ensure there is no existing admin
user if the person installing opts to "use an existing database".

Users installing PA can now opt to use a databes from an existing
PA install. They will only be allowed to enter a username and
password which can connect to the existing database. [#57 state:resolved]

Upon hitting next, the install process will ensure the user can log in
and has access to the database, and that the database is not empty.
If these conditions are met, then the installer assumes the db is filled
with an existing PA install, and then runs the update script packaged with
PA. In this way, brand-new PA installs can be set up to use the database from
older ones.

Adds installer options for meta-networking. Plus, it's pretty. [#39 state:resolved]

When installing, the installer now uses the result of trying to download
    - http://www.example.com/peopleaggregator.txt
    - http://example.com/peopleaggregator.txt
    - http://some-random-domain.example.com/peopleaggregator.txt
to determine if the server is compatible with meta-networking. If all three
downloads succeed, the installer presents the user with an option on the
following page to enable meta-networking. If any of the downloads fail,
it is assumed that meta-networking is not supported on this server due to the
install being on a subdomain.

Also, the installer tries to guess the domain_prefix value. If it guesses
incorrectly, the user can edit its value.

This commit adds some simple checks to make sure the variables
are set, before checking their values. If they're not set, the
checks do what would have already been done - as in, setting the
other variable to a null value, or continuing with the loop anyway.

Admins can now search for users' real names. [#16 status:resolved]

Adds SQL OR statements so admins, in manage_user.php, can now search for users' full names.
For example, a user with the id jdoe with first_name john and last_name doe
could be found by searching for any of the following:
	- jdoe
	- john
	- doe
	- john doe
